newsitem.title: singapore: Asian crude prices steady to lower, Dubai tightens.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude prices steady to lower, Dubai tightens.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady to lower on Friday, although Dubai intermonth spreads tighened amid dwindling supply in the wet market.
Middle East crudes appeared to find a trading range after the slump in premiums earlier this week.
Dubai intermonth spreads firmed amid dwindling Dubai supply for March. Traders said one cargo and a partial cargo were left on the shelf -- held by two European majors.
March/April firmed to 35/50 cents from a day-earlier 35/40, although the spread had started firming overnight in London with two deals done at +42 cents.
The firmer Dubai market was also reflected in the wet market.
A cargo changed hands among Japanese players at full-month quotes +53 cents and a second changed hands between a U.S. trader and a U.S. major at full-month quotes plus 51 cents.
However, traders said the last done was at +59 cents between a U.S. Wall Street trader and a U.S. major.
Bangchak Petroleum Plc awarded one Oman cargo in its March tender around MPM +10 cents to a Japanese trader, indicating Oman was finding a trading range around MPM +10 cents.

Other indications of steady levels came from the Qatar Marine market, where two deals involving majors were heard at QGPC +15 and QGPC +17 cents, although some traders suspected the latter deal was more like +15 cents.
A major continued to seek a buyer for first half February Tapis, offering at $1.20 or fixed price $24.50. Demand was slack however owing to weak margins on light sweet grades.
Most Tapis for February is done, although another major was said to be long of the market. March barrels were being assessed at a premium of 80/90 cents.
